chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah al-Nishapuri from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nishapuri from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Muthanna al-Hannat from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) say: 'The Qaim (the Rising One) will not rise until a caller from the sky calls, and the girl in her chamber will hear it, and the people of the East and the West will hear it.'
And regarding this, this verse was revealed: 'If We please, We should send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks should stoop to it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'caller from the sky' before the rise of Imam Mahdi?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration highlights the cosmic scale of the Mahdi’s emergence, where a heavenly caller’s voice penetrates even the most secluded spaces, ensuring universal awareness. The text explicitly links this phenomenon to Quran 26:4, interpreting the 'sign' as a divine auditory or visible miracle that compels all humanity, regardless of location, to bow in submission. This reflects the Shia eschatological view that the Mahdi’s rise is accompanied by undeniable, supernatural signs that transcend natural limitations.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 134 - It is narrated from Husain bin Ubaidullah from Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Sufyan Bazufari from Ahmad bin Idris from Ali bin Muhammad Ibn Qutaibah Nishapuri from Fadhl bin Shazan Nishapuri from Hasan bin Ali Ibn Faddal from Muthanna Hannat from Hasan bin Ziyad Saiqal that he said:
I heard Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) say: “Without any doubt, Imam Qaim (a.s) will not reappear till there is a call from the sky, which the ladies in veils and people of each corner of the world hear.
It is about this point that the following verse is revealed: “If We please, We should send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks should stoop to it.” [26:4]
